transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

So gentle gardening like light weeding or pottering about should be fine after that first week, but just take it easy and avoid anything too strenuous.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that helps! I was also wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be fine to keep using it as you were before. If you're not sure about the specific instructions, just check with your GP or the information that came with your drops.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm feeling very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It is quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. 

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. That should help.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It is quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:

If it's just mild sensitivity and things seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one last thing. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common to have blurry vision in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long has it been since your operation? If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's all for now. Thank you for answering my questions!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered them all. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
